questions.q: In which part of a plant cell does photosynthesis take place?
questions.qAf: In watter deel van 'n plantsel vind fotosintese plaas?
questions.explain: Photosynthesis happens in the chloroplasts, which contain the green pigment chlorophyll. Mitochondria are where cellular respiration happens.
questions.explainAf: Fotosintese vind in die chloroplaste plaas, wat die groen pigment chlorofil bevat. Mitochondria is waar sellulêre respirasie plaasvind.

questions.q: Why do most leaves look green to us?
questions.qAf: Waarom lyk die meeste blare vir ons groen?
options: Chlorophyll reflects green light and absorbs mainly red and blue light
Chlorophyll absorbs green light and reflects red and blue light
Leaves make green light during photosynthesis
Oxygen inside the leaf is green
optionsAf: Chlorofil weerkaats groen lig en absorbeer hoofsaaklik rooi en blou lig
Chlorofil absorbeer groen lig en weerkaats rooi en blou lig
Blare maak groen lig tydens fotosintese
Die suurstof in die blaar is groen
questions.explain: Chlorophyll absorbs mainly red and blue light. It reflects green light, and that reflected green light is what reaches your eye.
questions.explainAf: Chlorofil absorbeer hoofsaaklik rooi en blou lig. Dit weerkaats groen lig, en dié weerkaatste groen lig is wat jou oog bereik.

questions.q: Which sub-atomic particle has no charge and is found in the nucleus?
questions.qAf: Watter subatomiese deeltjie het geen lading nie en word in die kern gevind?
questions.explain: Neutrons are neutral and sit in the nucleus with the positive protons. Electrons are negative and orbit the nucleus in shells.
questions.explainAf: Neutrone is neutraal en is saam met die positiewe protone in die kern. Elektrone is negatief en wentel in doppe om die kern.

questions.q: Aluminium has an atomic number of 13 and a mass number of 27. How many neutrons are in one aluminium atom?
questions.qAf: Aluminium het 'n atoomgetal van 13 en 'n massagetal van 27. Hoeveel neutrone is in een aluminiumatoom?
questions.explain: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 27 − 13 = 14.
questions.explainAf: Neutrone = massagetal − atoomgetal = 27 − 13 = 14.

whyWrong.0: Gave the atomic number as the neutrons.
whyWrong.2: Gave the mass number instead of subtracting.
whyWrong.3: Added the mass number and atomic number (27 + 13).

whyWrongAf.0: Die atoomgetal as die neutrone gegee.
whyWrongAf.2: Die massagetal gegee in plaas van af te trek.
whyWrongAf.3: Die massagetal en atoomgetal bymekaar getel (27 + 13).

questions.q: Sodium has 11 electrons. What is its electron arrangement?
questions.qAf: Natrium het 11 elektrone. Wat is sy elektronrangskikking?
questions.explain: Shell 1 holds up to 2 electrons and shell 2 up to 8, so the 11th electron starts shell 3: 2,8,1.
questions.explainAf: Dop 1 hou tot 2 elektrone en dop 2 tot 8, dus begin die 11de elektron dop 3: 2,8,1.

questions.q: A plastic ruler is rubbed with wool and becomes negatively charged. What happened?
questions.qAf: 'n Plastiekliniaal word met wol gevryf en word negatief gelaai. Wat het gebeur?
options: The ruler gained electrons from the wool
The ruler gained protons from the wool
The ruler lost electrons to the wool
The ruler lost protons to the wool
optionsAf: Die liniaal het elektrone van die wol gekry
Die liniaal het protone van die wol gekry
Die liniaal het elektrone aan die wol verloor
Die liniaal het protone aan die wol verloor
questions.explain: Only electrons move when materials are rubbed. The material that gains electrons becomes negative; protons stay locked in the nucleus.
questions.explainAf: Slegs elektrone beweeg wanneer stowwe gevryf word. Die stof wat elektrone kry, word negatief; protone bly in die kern vasgevang.

questions.q: Why can sound not travel through outer space?
questions.qAf: Waarom kan klank nie deur die buitenste ruimte beweeg nie?
options: Sound needs a medium (particles) to travel through
Space is too cold for sound
Sound travels too slowly to cross space
optionsAf: Klank het 'n medium (deeltjies) nodig om deur te beweeg
Die ruimte is te koud vir klank
Klank beweeg te stadig om die ruimte oor te steek
questions.explain: Sound is a mechanical, longitudinal wave carried by vibrating particles. Space is a vacuum with no particles to carry it.
questions.explainAf: Klank is 'n meganiese, longitudinale golf wat deur vibrerende deeltjies gedra word. Die ruimte is 'n vakuum sonder deeltjies om dit te dra.

questions.q: A ray of light strikes a plane mirror with an angle of incidence of 35°. What is the angle of reflection?
questions.qAf: 'n Ligstraal tref 'n plat spieël met 'n invalshoek van 35°. Wat is die weerkaatsingshoek?
questions.explain: The law of reflection: the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, both measured from the normal.
questions.explainAf: Die wet van weerkaatsing: die invalshoek is gelyk aan die weerkaatsingshoek, albei gemeet vanaf die normaal.

questions.q: What keeps the planets in their orbits around the Sun?
questions.qAf: Wat hou die planete in hul wentelbane om die Son?
questions.explain: Gravity is the force of attraction between objects with mass. The Sun has 99.86% of the solar system's mass, and its gravity holds everything in orbit.
questions.explainAf: Swaartekrag is die aantrekkingskrag tussen voorwerpe met massa. Die Son het 99,86% van die sonnestelsel se massa, en sy swaartekrag hou alles in wentelbaan.

questions.q: Why was Pluto reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006?
questions.qAf: Waarom is Pluto in 2006 as 'n dwergplaneet geherklassifiseer?
options: It has not cleared the neighbourhood around its orbit
It does not orbit the Sun
optionsAf: Dit het nie die buurt rondom sy wentelbaan skoongemaak nie
Dit wentel nie om die Son nie
questions.explain: Pluto orbits the Sun in the Kuiper Belt, but it has not cleared the neighbourhood around its orbit, so it is a dwarf planet.
questions.explainAf: Pluto wentel in die Kuipergordel om die Son, maar dit het nie die buurt rondom sy wentelbaan skoongemaak nie, dus is dit 'n dwergplaneet.

sections.title: Give ONE word or term
sections.intro: Write ONE word or term for each description.
sections.introAf: Skryf EEN woord of term vir elke beskrywing.

questions.q: The process in which plants use light energy to make glucose.
questions.qAf: Die proses waarin plante ligenergie gebruik om glukose te maak.

questions.q: The smallest particle of an element that still has the properties of that element.
questions.qAf: Die kleinste deeltjie van ’n element wat steeds die eienskappe van daardie element het.

questions.q: An organism that breaks down dead plants and animals.
questions.qAf: ’n Organisme wat dooie plante en diere afbreek.

questions.q: A material that does not allow electric charges to move through it easily.
questions.qAf: ’n Materiaal wat nie elektriese ladings maklik deur hom laat beweeg nie.

questions.q: The path that a planet follows around the Sun.
questions.qAf: Die pad wat ’n planeet om die Son volg.

questions.q: A substance made of only one type of atom.
questions.qAf: ’n Stof wat uit net een soort atoom bestaan.

sections.title: Fill in the missing words
sections.intro: Type the word that is missing in each space.
sections.introAf: Tik die woord wat in elke spasie ontbreek.

questions.q: Fill in the missing words.
questions.qAf: Vul die ontbrekende woorde in.
questions.text: In respiration, glucose reacts with [[]] to release energy, carbon dioxide and [[]].
questions.textAf: Tydens respirasie reageer glukose met [[]] om energie, koolstofdioksied en [[]] vry te stel.

questions.q: Fill in the missing words.
questions.qAf: Vul die ontbrekende woorde in.
questions.text: A rubbed balloon sticks to a wall because of [[]] electricity. Like charges cause [[]] between objects.
questions.textAf: ’n Gevryfde ballon kleef aan ’n muur as gevolg van [[]] elektrisiteit. Gelyke ladings veroorsaak [[]] tussen voorwerpe.

questions.q: Fill in the missing words.
questions.qAf: Vul die ontbrekende woorde in.
questions.text: The Earth takes about [[]] days to orbit the Sun, and it spins once on its [[]] every 24 hours.
questions.textAf: Die Aarde neem ongeveer [[]] dae om om die Son te wentel, en dit draai elke 24 uur een keer om sy [[]].

sections.title: True or false
sections.intro: Decide whether each statement is true or false.
sections.introAf: Besluit of elke stelling waar of onwaar is.

questions.q: Cellular respiration only takes place during the day, when there is sunlight.
questions.qAf: Sellulêre respirasie vind net bedags plaas, wanneer daar sonlig is.
questions.explain: False. Respiration happens in all living cells 24 hours a day. It is photosynthesis that needs light.
questions.explainAf: Onwaar. Respirasie vind 24 uur per dag in alle lewende selle plaas. Dit is fotosintese wat lig nodig het.

questions.q: A virus needs a host cell to reproduce.
questions.qAf: 'n Virus het 'n gasheersel nodig om voort te plant.
questions.explain: True. Viruses cannot reproduce on their own, which is why they are not considered truly living.
questions.explainAf: Waar. Virusse kan nie op hul eie voortplant nie, en daarom word hulle nie as werklik lewend beskou nie.

questions.q: Elements in the same group of the periodic table have the same number of electrons in their outer shell.
questions.qAf: Elemente in dieselfde groep van die periodieke tabel het dieselfde aantal elektrone in hul buitenste dop.
questions.explain: True. That is why elements in a group have similar chemical properties. Group 1 elements all have 1 outer electron.
questions.explainAf: Waar. Daarom het elemente in 'n groep soortgelyke chemiese eienskappe. Groep 1-elemente het almal 1 buitenste elektron.

questions.q: In a chemical reaction, new atoms are created to make the products.
questions.qAf: In 'n chemiese reaksie word nuwe atome geskep om die produkte te maak.
questions.explain: False. Atoms are only rearranged. No atoms are created or destroyed, so mass is conserved.
questions.explainAf: Onwaar. Atome word net herrangskik. Geen atome word geskep of vernietig nie, dus bly massa behoue.

questions.q: A black object looks black because it absorbs all the colours of light.
questions.qAf: 'n Swart voorwerp lyk swart omdat dit al die kleure van lig absorbeer.
questions.explain: True. No light is reflected to your eye. A white object does the opposite: it reflects all colours.
questions.explainAf: Waar. Geen lig word na jou oog weerkaats nie. 'n Wit voorwerp doen die teenoorgestelde: dit weerkaats alle kleure.

sections.title: Matching
sections.intro: Match column A to column B, and find the matching pairs.
sections.introAf: Pas kolom A by kolom B, en vind die pare wat bymekaar pas.

questions.q: Match each type of micro-organism in column A with a disease it causes in column B.
questions.qAf: Pas elke soort mikro-organisme in kolom A by 'n siekte wat dit veroorsaak in kolom B.
questions.explain: Cholera is caused by bacteria (Vibrio cholerae), flu by the influenza virus, malaria by the protist Plasmodium, and athlete's foot by a fungus.
questions.explainAf: Cholera word deur bakterieë (Vibrio cholerae) veroorsaak, griep deur die influensavirus, malaria deur die protis Plasmodium, en voetskimmel deur 'n swam.

questions.q: Find the matching pairs: link each substance to the kind of matter it is.
questions.qAf: Vind die pare wat bymekaar pas: koppel elke stof aan die soort materie wat dit is.
questions.explain: O₂ contains only one type of atom, so it is an element. H₂O has two elements chemically bonded in a fixed ratio, so it is a compound. Air is gases physically mixed, not bonded, so it is a mixture.
questions.explainAf: O₂ bevat net een soort atoom, dus is dit 'n element. H₂O het twee elemente wat chemies in 'n vaste verhouding gebind is, dus is dit 'n verbinding. Lug is gasse wat fisies gemeng is, nie gebind nie, dus is dit 'n mengsel.

questions.q: Match each state of matter in column A with how its particles behave in column B.
questions.qAf: Pas elke toestand van materie in kolom A by hoe sy deeltjies optree in kolom B.
pairs: Particles move fast in all directions, far apart
pairsAf: Deeltjies beweeg vinnig in alle rigtings, ver uitmekaar
questions.explain: In a solid, particles vibrate in place; in a liquid, they slide past each other; in a gas, they move fast and far apart. Particles never stop moving.
questions.explainAf: In 'n vaste stof vibreer deeltjies in hul plek; in 'n vloeistof gly hulle by mekaar verby; in 'n gas beweeg hulle vinnig en ver uitmekaar. Deeltjies hou nooit op beweeg nie.

questions.q: Match each telescope in column A with its description in column B.
questions.qAf: Pas elke teleskoop in kolom A by sy beskrywing in kolom B.
pairs: An optical telescope at Sutherland in the Northern Cape
A radio telescope of 64 dishes in the Karoo
pairsAf: 'n Optiese teleskoop by Sutherland in die Noord-Kaap
'n Radioteleskoop met 64 skottels in die Karoo
'n Ruimteteleskoop wat om die Aarde wentel
questions.explain: SALT is the largest single optical telescope in the Southern Hemisphere. MeerKAT is the precursor to the SKA. Hubble orbits above the atmosphere, so its images are not blurred.
questions.explainAf: SALT is die grootste enkele optiese teleskoop in die Suidelike Halfrond. MeerKAT is die voorloper van die SKA. Hubble wentel bo die atmosfeer, dus is sy beelde nie vaag nie.

sections.title: Steps in order
sections.intro: Put the steps in the correct order.
sections.introAf: Plaas die stappe in die korrekte volgorde.

questions.q: Put the stages of electricity's journey from a power station to a home in the correct order.
questions.qAf: Plaas die fases van elektrisiteit se reis van 'n kragstasie na 'n huis in die korrekte volgorde.
steps: Generation at the power station (about 11–22 kV)
A step-up transformer increases the voltage (about 400 kV)
Transmission over long distances on pylons
A step-down transformer at a substation lowers the voltage
stepsAf: Oordrag oor lang afstande op kragmaste
'n Af-transformator by 'n substasie verlaag die spanning
questions.explain: Generate, step up, transmit, step down, distribute. A high voltage needs a lower current, so less energy is lost as heat in the long cables.
questions.explainAf: Wek op, stoot op, dra oor, stoot af, versprei. 'n Hoë spanning het 'n laer stroom nodig, dus gaan minder energie as hitte in die lang kabels verlore.

questions.q: Put these in order from smallest to largest.
questions.qAf: Plaas hierdie in volgorde van kleinste tot grootste.
questions.explain: Planet → planetary system (solar system) → galaxy → observable universe. The Milky Way holds 200–400 billion stars, and the universe about 2 trillion galaxies.
questions.explainAf: Planeet → planetêre stelsel (sonnestelsel) → sterrestelsel → waarneembare heelal. Die Melkweg bevat 200–400 miljard sterre, en die heelal ongeveer 2 triljoen sterrestelsels.

sections.title: Calculation and short answers
sections.intro: Show the answer in the box. For the written question you mark your own answer against the memo after you hand in.
sections.introAf: Gee die antwoord in die blokkie. Vir die geskrewe vraag merk jy jou eie antwoord teen die memorandum nadat jy ingehandig het.

questions.q: In a food chain, grass stores 10 000 kJ of energy. About 10% of the energy passes on to the next level. How much energy reaches a rabbit that eats the grass?
questions.qAf: In ’n voedselketting stoor gras 10 000 kJ energie. Ongeveer 10% van die energie gaan oor na die volgende vlak. Hoeveel energie bereik ’n haas wat die gras eet?

questions.q: Explain why a food web is more stable than a single food chain.
questions.qAf: Verduidelik waarom ’n voedselweb meer stabiel is as ’n enkele voedselketting.
points: If one food source disappears, the animals can eat other organisms in the web
So the loss of one species does not make the whole web collapse (other populations are less affected)
pointsAf: As een voedselbron verdwyn, kan die diere ander organismes in die web eet
Dus laat die verlies van een spesie nie die hele web ineenstort nie (ander bevolkings word minder geraak)

sections.title: Scenarios
sections.intro: Read each scenario, then answer the questions about it.
sections.introAf: Lees elke scenario en beantwoord dan die vrae daaroor.

questions.scenario: On a South African savanna, the grass in one area stores 20 000 kJ of energy. A simple food chain there is: Grass → Zebra → Lion. Use the 10% rule.
questions.scenarioAf: Op 'n Suid-Afrikaanse savanne stoor die gras in een gebied 20 000 kJ energie. 'n Eenvoudige voedselketting daar is: Gras → Sebra → Leeu. Gebruik die 10%-reël.

questions.q: About how much of the grass's energy is available to the zebras?
questions.qAf: Ongeveer hoeveel van die gras se energie is beskikbaar vir die sebras?
questions.explain: Only about 10% passes to the next trophic level: 10% of 20 000 kJ is 2 000 kJ.
questions.explainAf: Slegs ongeveer 10% gaan na die volgende trofiese vlak oor: 10% van 20 000 kJ is 2 000 kJ.
working: Only about 10% passes to the next trophic level.
workingAf: Net ongeveer 10% gaan na die volgende trofiese vlak.

whyWrong.0: Did not take any energy away: the full 20 000 kJ.
whyWrong.3: Took 10% twice: that is the energy for the lions.

whyWrongAf.0: Geen energie afgetrek nie: die volle 20 000 kJ.
whyWrongAf.3: 10% twee keer geneem: dit is die energie vir die leeus.

questions.q: About how much of the grass's energy reaches the lions?
questions.qAf: Ongeveer hoeveel van die gras se energie bereik die leeus?
questions.explain: 10% of the zebras' 2 000 kJ is 200 kJ. Energy is lost at every level through respiration, movement and heat.
questions.explainAf: 10% van die sebras se 2 000 kJ is 200 kJ. Energie gaan by elke vlak verlore deur respirasie, beweging en hitte.
workingAf: Neem 10% van die sebras se 2 000 kJ.

whyWrong.0: Took only one step: the zebras’ 2 000 kJ.
whyWrong.1: Halved the energy instead of taking 10%.
whyWrong.3: Took 10% three times, one step too many.

whyWrongAf.0: Net een stap geneem: die sebras se 2 000 kJ.
whyWrongAf.1: Die energie gehalveer in plaas van 10% te neem.
whyWrongAf.3: 10% drie keer geneem, een stap te veel.

questions.q: What is the zebra's role in this food chain?
questions.qAf: Wat is die sebra se rol in hierdie voedselketting?
questions.explain: The zebra is a herbivore that eats the producer (grass), so it is a primary consumer on the 2nd trophic level.
questions.explainAf: Die sebra is 'n herbivoor wat die produsent (gras) eet, dus is dit 'n primêre verbruiker op die 2de trofiese vlak.

questions.q: There are far fewer lions than zebras on the savanna because so much energy is lost at each trophic level.
questions.qAf: Daar is baie minder leeus as sebras op die savanne omdat soveel energie by elke trofiese vlak verlore gaan.
questions.explain: True. The energy that reaches the top predators is too small to support large numbers of them.
questions.explainAf: Waar. Die energie wat die toproofdiere bereik, is te min om groot getalle van hulle te onderhou.

questions.scenario: A learner builds a circuit with a 6 V battery, a switch, an ammeter and a 3 Ω resistor. Use Ohm's law: V = I × R.
questions.scenarioAf: 'n Leerder bou 'n stroombaan met 'n 6 V-battery, 'n skakelaar, 'n ampèremeter en 'n 3 Ω-resistor. Gebruik die Wet van Ohm: V = I × R.

questions.q: What current flows in the circuit?
questions.qAf: Watter stroom vloei in die stroombaan?

whyWrong.0: Divided the resistance by the voltage (3 ÷ 6) the wrong way round.
whyWrong.2: Gave the resistance (3 Ω) as the current.

whyWrongAf.0: Die weerstand deur die spanning gedeel (3 ÷ 6) – die verkeerde kant toe.
whyWrongAf.2: Die weerstand (3 Ω) as die stroom gegee.

questions.q: The learner swaps the resistor for a 6 Ω one, with the same battery. What is the current now?
questions.qAf: Die leerder ruil die resistor om vir 'n 6 Ω-resistor, met dieselfde battery. Wat is die stroom nou?
questions.explain: I = 6 ÷ 6 = 1 A. More resistance means less current.
questions.explainAf: I = 6 ÷ 6 = 1 A. Meer weerstand beteken minder stroom.
working: I = V ÷ R with the new R = 6 Ω.
workingAf: I = V ÷ R met die nuwe R = 6 Ω.

whyWrong.1: Kept the old current of 2 A instead of working out the new one.

whyWrongAf.1: Die ou stroom van 2 A behou in plaas van die nuwe een uit te werk.

questions.q: How must the ammeter be connected to measure the current?
questions.qAf: Hoe moet die ampèremeter gekoppel word om die stroom te meet?
options: It does not need to be connected
optionsAf: Dit hoef nie gekoppel te word nie
questions.explain: An ammeter measures current, so it goes in series, in the loop. A voltmeter is connected in parallel.
questions.explainAf: 'n Ampèremeter meet stroom, dus word dit in serie in die lus gekoppel. 'n Voltmeter word in parallel gekoppel.

questions.q: The lights in the learner's home are wired in parallel, so if one bulb breaks, the others stay on.
questions.qAf: Die ligte in die leerder se huis is in parallel bedraad, dus as een gloeilamp breek, bly die ander aan.
questions.explain: True. In a parallel circuit each bulb has its own path, so the others keep working. In a series circuit they would all go out.
questions.explainAf: Waar. In 'n parallelle stroombaan het elke gloeilamp sy eie pad, dus werk die ander aan. In 'n seriestroombaan sou hulle almal afgaan.
